messages:
alice: Heads up — canary p95 latency jumped ~2.5x after yesterday's merge (r2026.03.17 / PR #4521). Seeing compile storms and GPU OOM-ish behavior on small-batch chat workloads. Anyone watching?

deploy-bot: canary deploy r2026.03.17 completed 2026-03-17T09:12:03Z. Health checks passed initially.

ben: I pulled the canary node logs. Lots of repeated kernel compiles and cache evictions. Looks like the autotuner is picking a new quantized GEMM kernel for short sequences which is slower due to compile latency.

carol: Can you paste the compile logs?

ben: Sure — shortened: 
```
[2026-03-17T09:14:22Z] compile: model=redwood-7b variant=quant4 kernel=gemm_quant4_v2
[2026-03-17T09:14:22Z] compile_time=12.3s cache_hit=false
[2026-03-17T09:14:23Z] kvcache: mark_dirty tag=autopick_gemm_quant4_v2
[2026-03-17T09:14:30Z] evict: kv_entries=127 reason=tag_invalidate
[2026-03-17T09:14:35Z] compile: repeated compile storm for same kernel across shards
```
This pattern repeats across shards and saturates the driver compile queue.

diana: That tag_invalidate is suspicious. We changed autopick tag format in the autotune heuristic last week (PR #4489). It might be generating ephemeral keys that bypass the kernel cache.

eric: Quick check: prod-ctr workload doesn't see this because it usually hits the cached fp16 kernel. Canary uses a different seq-dist and triggered the new heuristic.

alice: So cause hypothesis: new autotune rule favored gemm_quant4_v2 for predicted compute efficiency, but the kernel module is not in the shared cache (or the tag differs), leading to simultaneous compiles and KV cache invalidation -> compile storm -> evictions -> latency spike.

carol: Can we bisect to identify the exact commit that changed how autotune tags kernels? I can run rk-bisect later today.

ben: I started a quick local bisect against main~12..main using p95_latency on the perf harness. Initial result points at commit abc1234 (PR #4489) which changed autotune:key_format and added quant heuristics.

diana: Confirmed. The change moved from using (arch, kernel_name) to (arch, kernel_name, heuristic_version) and forgot to normalize quant variant names. So runtime treats the same kernel as different keys across minor name diffs.

ben: Repro script (fast):
```bash
# repro run on canary image
./run_local_perf --model redwood-7b --seq 64 --batch 4 --workload chat --trace compile_logs > out.log
grep "compile: model" out.log | head -n 20
```
You can see repeated compile_time ~12s entries for gemm_quant4_v2 with cache_hit=false.

eric: Also note KV cache evictions are triggered because compiled-code tag touches the KV cache keyspace in our implementation. The new tag churn causes frequent invalidations.

alice: We need an immediate mitigation to stop canary from degrading and unblock rollout. Options: 1) revert PR #4489 (fast), 2) pin autopick to previous heuristic via runtime flag, 3) add a short-lived global compile semaphore to rate-limit compiles. Thoughts?

diana: Revert is fastest. I'll open a revert CL and roll back the autotune tag change. We should also add a unit test for tag normalization.

carol: Meanwhile, we can flip a runtime feature flag on canary to force kernel_selection_mode=legacy (ben, can you patch the canary config?).

ben: Patching canary to kernel_selection_mode=legacy now... 

deploy-bot: config update applied to canary: kernel_selection_mode=legacy at 2026-03-17T09:43:01Z by ben.

ben: After the flip, compile storms dropped immediately and p95 returned to baseline within ~2 minutes. Monitoring shows evict_count went from 127/min to ~2/min.

alice: Great. Diana — please land the revert CL and link it here. Also add a follow-up to rework autotune tagging so it normalizes quant variants and doesn't include volatile heuristic_version values.

diana: Revert PR opened: revert/4489 (CL 0f3a1b). Patch note: revert autotune tag formatting and add defensive normalization + unit test. Requesting rapid review.

eric: Longer-term: we should change the compile cache key design so that invalidation isn't coupled to kernel tag churn, and add a compile-rate limiter to the runtime to prevent simultaneous cold compiles from causing OOM/latency blips. Filing tracking ticket INF-728 (perf infra).

alice: Owner list/next steps: diana -> land revert CL (urgent), ben -> keep canary pinned to legacy until revert lands, carol -> add regression test in perf harness that simulates tag churn, eric -> proposal for cache key refactor + compile semaphore.

ben: I'll keep watching metrics and will escalate if anything else pops up.

carol: Left a note in the release channel and updated the rollout checklist.

alice: Thanks all. Closing the loop once revert is green. :thumbsup:
